chapters.text: This is Nota. It turns an AI trading opinion into something you can check, instead of something you have to trust.
The mark is not decoration. Its ticks are the evidence hash of a real receipt, and the arc is the probability that receipt's judge stated. The same evidence always draws the same figure.
The headline claims a decision can be re-run. So let's press the button and check it, live.
Identical, true. That rebuilt the decision from the stored evidence and the model output cached beside it. No key, no network call to any model.

Nota also audits the data it is given. It recomputes RYO's own RSI and ATR from public candles with Wilder's method. Four point three four seven against RYO's four point three seven six: zero point six seven percent apart.
Four receipts ship with the repository, each drawing itself from its own hash.
Every receipt opens on a thirty second summary. What was decided, what changed most since the previous receipt, where the practice position stands, and what happens next.
Each receipt is diffed against the one before it for the same symbol, and ranked by impact, so the row that mattered is the row on top.

Three specialists argue. Each cites dotted paths into the evidence, and the value shown is read back out of that evidence rather than retyped by the model. A citation pointing at something absent is dropped in code, and the opinion is downgraded for it.
Four research skills run from this panel, and the same four are served over the Model Context Protocol, so Claude Desktop or Cursor can call them directly.
Read-only research on RYO evidence. No order is ever placed. Not financial advice.
